production_sources.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production original hand-drawn 2D videogame WALK animation sprite sheet. Input image is CHARACTER IDENTITY REFERENCE ONLY. Keep exactly this clerk: cobalt blue hair with coral front streak and yellow highlights, turquoise eyes, cropped yellow/navy courier jacket with white cuff band and planet sleeve badge, navy shorts with yellow pocket details, bare lower legs and navy/yellow/cream ankle boots. Remove the tablet for walking; no props. Preserve age appearance, face design, body and head proportions, colors and polished cartoon ink rendering; NO 3D. Create precisely EIGHT DISTINCT full-body frames in a clean 4 columns by 2 rows sheet, left-to-right then next row. Every figure faces RIGHT in the same three-quarter SIDE VIEW, same camera, same anatomy scale, same hip horizontal position within its cell. Generous transparent gaps; truly transparent background; no shadows, no floor, no text, no labels. This is a coherent complete regular WALK, not a run: upright torso, slight controlled bounce, modest arm counter-swing, one boot always touching a shared imaginary baseline. Frame1 NEAR LEG CONTACT: near leg reaches forward heel on floor toe slightly up, far leg stretched back toe on floor; far arm forward near arm back. Frame2 NEAR LEG DOWN: body lowered a little, near support boot now flat and forward of hip, near knee softly bent; far boot lifted behind with knee bent. Frame3 NEAR LEG PASSING: near support leg nearly vertical beneath hip, boot flat on floor; far knee moving forward with far boot clearly airborne passing next to support ankle; arms passing each other. Frame4 NEAR LEG UP: body slightly higher, near support leg extends backward with heel lifted and toe still on floor; far knee and boot swing forward above floor; near arm forward. Frame5 FAR LEG CONTACT: exact opposite limbs to frame1, FAR leg now forward heel touching floor, NEAR leg back toe touching; NEAR arm forward, far arm back. Frame6 FAR LEG DOWN: far boot flat slightly forward of hips carries weight, near boot lifted behind, body lower. Frame7 FAR LEG PASSING: far support leg vertical boot flat below hip, near knee swings forward with near boot off floor; arms passing. Frame8 FAR LEG UP: far support leg behind toe on floor, near leg swings forward preparing frame1. The visible pocket and overlapping limbs must make left/right alternation unmistakable. Feet must trace a continuous backwards ground path from front to underneath to behind during EACH support half; do not repeat wide scissor contact for passing frames. Keep consistent boot size, face size and limb length in all eight. Full hair tips and all boots fit in each cell. Quality: strong readable key poses and accurate biomechanics, not just eight charming similar poses.
production_sources.inspection_result: The eight-drawing sheet did not reliably alternate anatomical leg identity. Selected intact generated pixels were therefore segmented and articulated into explicit alternating legs; the raw eight-frame sheet is not claimed to be a finished cycle.

production_sources.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Production 2D character animation sheet for existing original courier clerk, exactly matching this reference identity and outfit, with the tablet removed. A DISTINCT fast RUN CYCLE, not walking. 8 frames in 4 columns x 2 rows on TRANSPARENT background. Full-body characters consistently face right in a SIDE VIEW with a slight three-quarter face. All eight same body scale, identical head size and hair silhouette. Deep blue hair with coral forelock, cyan eyes, yellow/navy cropped jacket with pale cuff and planet badge, navy shorts yellow pockets, bare shins, chunky yellow/cream/navy boots. Sharp clean outlined 2D raster illustration, no 3D. The torso noticeably leans 15 degrees FORWARD through the entire run, elbows bent, powerful opposite arm swing. Top row: 1 near-foot forward touchdown under bent knee with far heel kicked up behind; 2 near-leg compression, planted near boot now directly beneath hip and body lower, far thigh recovering forward; 3 near-foot toe-off behind with far knee raised forward; 4 FLIGHT both boots clearly airborne, far boot reaching forward and near heel tucked high back, body lifted. Bottom row: 5 far-foot forward touchdown and near heel kicked behind, NEAR ARM NOW FORWARD; 6 far-leg compression planted far foot beneath hip, near knee recovering forward; 7 far-foot toe-off behind and near knee raised forward; 8 FLIGHT both boots airborne, near foot reaching forward and far heel tucked back. Very important: alternate which anatomical leg is in front at the second contact, do not redraw the same leading leg. The near side pocket and near arm must move oppositely so support-leg swap is clear. Grounded frames1,2,3,5,6,7 meet a common imaginary floor; airborne frames4,8 genuinely elevated. Large knee flexion, heel recovery, short planted stance, energetic forward lean. Consistent foot shapes and length of limbs, elegant continuity between poses. Transparent background with no gradient, no cast shadow, no floor, no lettering or frame borders; generous spacing between figures.
production_sources.inspection_result: Distinct lean and bent-arm identity were useful. Leading-leg identity still repeated in parts of the raw sheet. Production uses the clean forward-leaning torso plus explicit near/far raster leg articulation and measured flight intervals.

derivation: build_raster_rig.py masks/crops generated torso, sleeve and complete limb regions, rotates raster parts using their own measured 2D joint lengths, and emits32 samples per gait. register_runtime.py applies one common final similarity transform, binary alpha and the existing96-color palette. Runtime uses a bounded lower-body sampling shift to cancel actual travelled distance during support. No character pixels are painted procedurally, and no Spine or3D assets are present.
